column1: # What the odi-oss image does with each config key. Hand-written, per image,
# and the reason the UI shows 21 keys instead of 184: a key with no row here is
# read by nothing on this image. It stays in the store, and in backups and
# restores, because the config partition is shared with the stock firmware in
# the other slot, which does read it -- but it is not offered for editing.
# apply    what applying costs, shown beside the key:
#            live      takes effect at once, no interruption
#            restart   a daemon restarts; the fibre service stays up
#            internet  applied without a reboot, but the fibre service drops
#                      while it is (the ONU re-ranges and is provisioned again)
#            reboot    only at the next boot, which also drops the service
# action   what the page runs to apply it: network (apply.sh network), omci
#          (apply.sh omci), reboot. confd reports the actions a save needs.
# pair     shown read-only and written together with the named key
# reader   what on the image reads it
# note     why it costs what it does
# Source of truth for the classes: odi-oss docs/SETTINGS.md. scripts/check-schema.py
# checks every name against keys.tsv and every class and action against the lists

omcid tags only with type 1 and manual mode 1, as the stock firmware does. Applying restarts omcid and re-ranges the ONU so the OLT provisions every service again.
See VLAN config mode.

Sent to the kernel before the ONU ranges; applying re-ranges it with the new one.
Answered to CTC-profile OLTs in the LOID authentication entity. Written with LOID_OLD, because the OLD value wins whenever the two differ.
Written with LOID_PASSWD_OLD, for the same reason.
Follows LOID.

Reported only while the OLT identity switch is on; otherwise 0.0.0. The stock firmware may rewrite this key when it boots.

Needs a reboot: the MAC is set on eth0 and its host port with the links down, before br0 exists, and doing that live would cut every way in mid-change.

Applying restarts syslogd (init respawns it with the new address); the fibre service is not touched.
Applying restarts ntpd (init respawns it with the new server); the fibre service is not touched.
